Brother '''Letrun Pay''' was an [[alien]] [[Gender|male]]<ref name="TLJVD" /> who spent time in the [[city]] of [[Canto Bight]]<ref name="TLJ" /> on the [[planet]] [[Cantonica]] in the [[Standard year|year]] [[34 ABY]].<ref name="Date">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' places the events of the film [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']] in [[34 ABY]]. As [[Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VIII ''The Last Jedi'']] carries on immediately from the events of ''The Force Awakens'', it can be assumed to take place in the same [[Standard year|year]].</ref> He stood at a railing looking out over the edge of the city and speaking to a [[human]] female when a [[fathier]] carrying the [[Resistance]] agents [[Finn]] and [[Rose Tico]] crashed through an archway behind him at high speed and leaped over the railing. Pay recoiled in surprise at the sudden appearance of the fathier, which was followed by a herd of riderless fathiers also fleeing the city. Pay had [[Color|blue]], light-sensitive [[eye]]s which he shielded with over-sized [[droptac]]s. He had white and pink skin and wore the white and black [[Vestments of the Sacred Circle]].<ref name="TLJ" />

==Behind the scenes==
Letrun Pay was portrayed by creature and droid performer [[Dee Tails]]<ref name="Twitter">{{Twitter|deetails|status/952563909847896064|[[Dee Tails]]|quote=This is another creature I got to play in The Last Jedi. He also appears in Canto Bight but very briefly. His name is Brother Letrun Pay.|archivefile=File:Dee_Tails_Letrun_Pay.png}}</ref> in the film [[Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VIII ''The Last Jedi'']],<ref name="TLJ" /> but prior to its release on [[December 15]], [[2017]],<ref name="Release Date">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-episode-viii-to-open-december-15-2017|text=''Star Wars: Episode VIII'' to Open December 15, 2017}}</ref> the character was revealed in an [[People Magazine Collector's Edition - Star Wars: The Ultimate Guide to The Last Jedi|issue]] of [[Wikipedia:People magazine|People magazine]]. Neither the magazine<ref name="People">''[[People Magazine Collector's Edition - Star Wars: The Ultimate Guide to The Last Jedi]]''</ref> or film<ref name="TLJ" /> revealed Pay's name, and he was first identified in ''[[Star Wars: The Last Jedi: The Visual Dictionary]]'', a reference book written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]]<ref name="TLJVD" /> and released the same day as the film.<ref name="Release date">{{SW|url=news/new-star-wars-the-last-jedi-books-and-more-revealed-at-sdcc-2017|text=New ''Star Wars: The Last Jedi'' Books and More Revealed at SDCC 2017}}</ref>
